stem.text: Genes have a role in determining the overall phenotype of an organism.
Using haemophilia as an example, explain the relationship between a gene, a protein and a phenotype.

points.text: a gene codes for a protein which determines the phenotype ;
(so) blood does not clot quickly enough / excessive bleeding occurs (after an injury) ;
link the phenotype to the genotype ;

examples: prevents activation of thrombin / fibrinogen not converted to fibrin
different mutations cause a range of severity of haemophilia

explanation.text: The F8 gene is on the X chromosome and codes for the protein factor VIII, which is needed for blood to clot. A recessive allele of F8 codes for a non-functional (or reduced/absent) factor VIII, so blood fails to clot quickly enough and bleeding after injury is excessive: this is the haemophilia phenotype.

Because the gene is X-linked, genotype and phenotype link up differently in males and females: XFXF and XFXf females are unaffected (one normal allele is enough), XfXf females are affected, XFY males are unaffected and XfY males are affected (a male has only one X, so one recessive allele is enough to cause the phenotype).

reasoningChain: State the general rule: a gene codes for a protein, and the protein (or its absence) produces the phenotype.
Apply it to haemophilia: F8 gene (X-linked) codes for factor VIII.
The recessive allele gives non-functional/less/no factor VIII, so clotting is impaired.
Link each genotype (XFXF, XFXf, XfXf, XFY, XfY) to whether the person is affected.

inferredMistakes.text: Describing haemophilia symptoms without first stating the general gene → protein → phenotype relationship the question asks for.
Forgetting that males need only one copy of the recessive allele to be affected, because the F8 gene is on the X chromosome and males are XY.

stem.text: In the pea plant, Pisum sativum, the genotype lele results in plants with short stems (dwarf plants).
Explain how the lele genotype and its gene product results in dwarf plants.

points.text: le/le is, homozygous recessive / two recessive alleles ;

alternatives: no / less, stem elongation / increase in internodal length ;

examples: ref. to GA 3β-hydroxylase / GA3-oxidase / last enzyme in the pathway that produces, active gibberellin / GA1
le allele codes for alanine instead of threonine (in the enzyme)

explanation.text: lele is homozygous recessive, so both copies of the gene code for a non-functional enzyme (one of the enzymes in the gibberellin synthesis pathway, e.g. GA 3β-hydroxylase / GA3-oxidase). Without a working enzyme, no active gibberellin (GA1) is produced, and since gibberellin normally promotes cell elongation, its absence means less cell and stem elongation, giving a short (dwarf) stem.

reasoningChain: lele = homozygous recessive, so no functional allele is present.
The le allele codes for a non-functional enzyme in the gibberellin synthesis pathway.
Without gibberellin, cells/internodes do not elongate as much, so the plant is dwarf.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying 'no gibberellin is made' instead of 'no active gibberellin/enzyme produced', missing that the block is an enzyme in gibberellin's synthesis pathway rather than the hormone's receptor or action.

stem.text: Dwarf plants also occur if the genes controlling growth are not activated (switched on).
Explain how DELLA proteins act as repressors preventing gene expression.

points.text: (DELLA proteins) bind to, PIF / transcription factor ;
PIF / transcription factor, cannot bind to, DNA / promoter ;
RNA polymerase cannot bind to promoter ;

explanation.text: DELLA proteins repress gene expression by binding directly to PIF transcription factors, stopping PIF from binding to its target gene's promoter. Without PIF bound to the promoter, RNA polymerase cannot bind there either, so transcription cannot start and no mRNA is made from that gene.

reasoningChain: DELLA protein binds to the PIF transcription factor.
Bound PIF cannot bind to the gene's promoter.
RNA polymerase then cannot bind to the promoter either.
Transcription (and hence mRNA production) does not happen.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying DELLA proteins bind directly to DNA/the promoter, when the MS specifies DELLA binds to the PIF transcription factor, which is what normally binds the promoter.
